text: Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement Solve zero-pressure planar, cylindrical and spherical Noh flow with 1D finite volumes. Compare exact cell means, origin heating and refinement; separately verify discrete budgets and boundary-time-quadrature error in spherical flow. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-noh-2026-11-23-r5 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Noh shocks: zero-pressure planar, cylindrical and spherical flow An original small 1D finite-volume code solves zero-pressure Noh flow in planar, cylindrical and spherical symmetry. Grids 64/128/256/512 measure full-domain error, origin heating, shock location and budgets, and compare spherical boundary-inflow time-quadrature error with its analytic identity. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Nondimensional r in [0,1], gamma=5/3, rho0=1, u0=-1, p0=0, T=.6. PDE runs use planar d=1, cylindrical-radial d=2 and spherical-radial d=3, with shock radius .2. Outer density is (1+t)^(d-1), the origin reflects, and the measure is r^(d-1)dr. The same angular factor is omitted throughout; spherical analytic totals are M=512/375 and E=256/375. Its figure is a central section of a 1D radial solution, not a Cartesian 2D/3D calculation or a test of angular symmetry breaking. Editorial clarification The initial failed attempt retains its source, inputs, diagnostic logs and all eight original full-field profile CSVs. These arrays are distinct from the failed summary recovered verbatim from stdout; their hashes match the same CSVs in the prior r3 edition. The successful release supplies all profiles, histories, results and an independently extracted ZIP rerun. Adopted numerical method Rusanov flux with SSPRK2 (Heun). Planar/cylindrical runs retain piecewise-constant reconstruction. Spherical runs reconstruct conserved variables linearly around volume centroids with minmod slopes based on centroid distances in interior cells and zero slopes in the two boundary cells. A single theta per cell scales all conserved slopes at both faces to check face density/internal energy. Cell means are never corrected and no pressure seed/floor is used. Wave speeds, Rusanov flux and numerical stress P*=F_mom-((u_L+u_R)/2)F_mass use the same face states. The geometric CFL V/(A_La_L+A_Ra_R) uses the prescribed .35. Spherical source quadrature exactly integrates the face-linear numerical stress against 2r dr; planar/cylindrical runs keep the old arithmetic rule. Reconstructed reflection faces use even/odd parity, with physical cold inflow at the outer face. The initial cylindrical failure retains its source, all eight diagnostic logs and failed summary; the face-stress revision was tested against the same gates. Analytic conserved means split shock-crossing integrals and distinguish p(mean U) from mean p. The pinned independent LANL ExactPack analytic comparison includes d=1/2/3. New spherical PDE refinements separately measure full-domain r^2-weighted L1/L2/Linf, density L1 in r<=.70rs including the origin, and center/shock/plateau diagnostics. Discrete stage-weighted inflow budgets are distinct from continuous analytic totals; SSPRK2 boundary quadrature is checked through M_h-M_exact=sum(dt^3)/6 and E_h-E_exact=sum(dt^3)/12. The first spherical run retained arithmetic source quadrature and failed two of 105 gates (finest shock-position error 3.923 cells, plateau-density error 11.03%); all results are retained. A second attempt changed only spherical stress quadrature, but still failed the same two gates (3.919 cells and 11.018% density error). A third attempt retains that quadrature and adds MUSCL/minmod reconstruction only for spherical runs, against the same 105 criteria. The third attempt completed 28 tests and all 12 grid runs, passing all 105 gates. At spherical N=512 the whole-domain density L1 is .0114343, shock error 1.98856 cells, plateau-density error 5.2533%, and origin-inclusive core-density L1 .0549503. Maximum center specific-internal-energy excess is 20.59%, worse than the second attempt's 15.52%; not every diagnostic improves. Verification limits and failures An educational calculation: first-order space in planar/cylindrical flow and MUSCL-type limited linear reconstruction in spherical flow. Origin heating and finite-grid plateau errors remain; the center is never removed from whole-domain error. Because r^2 weighting can make central defects appear small, an origin-inclusive fixed-core norm and enlarged view are also shown. Vanishing Linf/center maximum error, high order for the complete method on smooth spherical problems, general stage positivity with the geometric source, Cartesian multidimensional flow and independent arbitrary-gamma validation are not established. Cylindrical Linf was not monotone in the old series; spherical L2/Linf and heating are retained as diagnostics. Roundoff-scale discrete mass/energy balance coexists with O(dt^2) spherical boundary-time-quadrature error against analytic totals. Radial momentum has a geometric source and is not a conserved Cartesian momentum component. ExactPack independently implements the analytic evaluator, not another numerical PDE engine.
